short: Current assets divided by current liabilities.
seoTitle: Current Ratio — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: The current ratio divides current assets by current liabilities to measure whether a business can meet its short-term obligations from short-term resources.
definition: The current ratio divides current assets by current liabilities to measure whether a business can meet its short-term obligations from short-term resources. A ratio near or below one signals strain.
bodyHtml:
Why Current Ratio matters

It is the first liquidity check a lender runs. It is also easy to misread, because a high ratio built on unsold stock and uncollected invoices is not real strength.

Current Ratio formula

Current ratio = Current assets ÷ Current liabilities

Compare it against the quick ratio to see how much depends on inventory.

How Current Ratio works in practice

Read it with the quick ratio and with stock ageing. If the gap between the two ratios is wide, most of the apparent liquidity is stock rather than cash.

faq.question: What is a good current ratio?
faq.answer: Comfortably above one for most trading businesses, with the right level varying by sector and credit cycle.

faq.question: Can the ratio be too high?
faq.answer: Yes. It can indicate idle cash, excess stock or receivables nobody is chasing.
